question: Do directional conflicts among physics, boundary, and data losses explain PINN optimization failure, and can approximate second-order preconditioning resolve them at useful scale?

key_findings.claim: The proposed multi-gradient alignment score detects persistent intra- and inter-step conflict in PINNs trained with first-order optimizers.
key_findings.evidence: On Navier-Stokes and additional PDEs, transformed Adam/GD gradients oscillate near or below zero while quasi-second-order methods maintain more positive alignment and faster error reduction.

key_findings.claim: The theoretical account connects Hessian preconditioning to aligned successive updates and characterizes SOAP as an approximate block-diagonal Gauss-Newton/Newton step in a rotating Kronecker basis.
key_findings.evidence: The main propositions and Appendix D contrast diagonal Adam, Kronecker Shampoo, Muon, Kron and SOAP; the approximation relies on local smoothness and factorization assumptions.

key_findings.claim: SOAP reports the best relative L2 error across ten PDE benchmarks, including high-Reynolds cavity and Kolmogorov flows, with roughly two- to tenfold error reductions over baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 3-4 and the benchmark table compare Adam, Adam plus L-BFGS, Kron, Muon and SOAP; the reported turbulent cases use time marching, hard constraints, sampling and architecture choices detailed in the appendix.

key_findings.claim: The accuracy gain is not a free optimizer substitution: SOAP takes about twice the training time, and the strongest turbulent results combine it with substantial PINN-specific engineering.
key_findings.evidence: The cost discussion reports the slowdown, while Appendix G adds PirateNet, exact periodic constraints, Fourier features, curriculum/time marching, sampling and carefully selected beta/update frequencies.

method.core_idea: Treat PINN composite-loss optimization as a multi-objective direction-conflict problem and test whether curvature-aware preconditioners align the effective gradients.
method.mechanism: Measure alignment after each optimizer's transformation, analyze Hessian-preconditioned dynamics, and benchmark SOAP's rotating Kronecker eigenbasis across PDEs and architectures.
assumptions: Relative L2 error against numerical references is accurate and comparable across methods.
Local Hessian/Gauss-Newton structure is sufficiently captured by SOAP's block factorization.
The selected PINN architecture and training curriculum do not confound the optimizer comparison beyond reported ablations.

techniques.role: Generalizes pairwise cosine diagnostics to several composite-loss directions.
Runs Adam-like moments in a periodically updated Shampoo eigenbasis.
Evaluates first- and second-order methods across ten stiff and turbulent systems.

evaluations.setting: Ten PDE benchmarks from waves and reaction-diffusion to lid-driven cavity, Kolmogorov and Rayleigh-Taylor flows.
evaluations.metric: Relative L2 solution error, convergence trajectory, alignment score and runtime.
evaluations.result: SOAP is best in the reported table and reaches cases where Adam fails, at roughly twice baseline training time.
evaluations.baseline: Adam, Adam+L-BFGS, Muon, Kron, ConFIG and architecture/hyperparameter ablations.

limitations: Runtime-normalized superiority is less clear than convergence/error superiority.
The Newton approximation is local and block-factored rather than an exact full-Hessian equivalence.
Turbulent cases require multiple training interventions beyond the optimizer.
Benchmarks use deterministic references and do not quantify model-form or measurement uncertainty.
failure_modes: Stale or inaccurate preconditioner eigenbases can misalign gradients.
Second-order overhead can dominate when moderate accuracy is sufficient.
Composite-loss alignment can improve while the PDE solution remains physically wrong due to inadequate sampling or boundary enforcement.
reusable_insights: Gradient-conflict diagnostics should be computed after optimizer transformations, not only on raw loss gradients.
PINN optimizer studies must report the entire training stack because constraints and sampling can be as decisive as preconditioning.
Accuracy and equal-time frontiers are distinct claims.
open_questions: Can low-rank or infrequently updated SOAP retain the gain at Adam-like wall-clock cost?
Does alignment prospectively predict which PDE/architecture combinations will fail?
How does the method behave with noisy experimental observations and inverse problems?

competitive_landscape.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
competitive_landscape.relationship: Optimizer foundation used by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: The SOAP paper derives the rotated-Adam algorithm and tests language pretraining; the target interprets it through PINN gradient alignment and extends evaluation to stiff PDE solvers.

competitive_landscape.title: ConFIG: Towards Conflict-free Training of Physics Informed Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: ConFIG explicitly constructs a direction with positive dot product to each objective gradient; the target argues approximate curvature preconditioning resolves conflict implicitly and compares both.

competitive_landscape.title: Achieving High Accuracy with PINNs via Energy Natural Gradients
competitive_landscape.difference: Energy natural gradient uses a Hessian-induced function-space metric and obtains very high accuracy; the target emphasizes a scalable Kronecker approximation and a multi-gradient diagnostic over broader turbulent cases.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding and mitigating gradient pathologies in physics-informed neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. address imbalanced gradient magnitudes with adaptive weights and architecture changes; the target focuses on directional conflict and second-order alignment.

novelty_assessment: The strong contribution is joining a multi-objective alignment diagnostic to a modern scalable preconditioner and demonstrating a broad PINN accuracy frontier. Curvature-aware PINN methods and explicit conflict-free updates already exist, so novelty lies in the SOAP connection and empirical breadth, not in first identifying gradient pathologies.
